subject: Week 44: book the birthday photographer — SF lead times run 2-4 months
bodyText:
This week
Days 306–312: walking is the dominant motor question — emerging for some, with standing alone momentarily at the CDC 12-month checkpoint — and falls are part of the practice loop. He is imitating familiar actions, using objects intentionally, and understands "no" (CDC 12-month); first specific words remain emerging for some, with the CDC 2022 checkpoint for words beyond mama/dada at 15 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Falls during walking practice — forehead and shin bruises are the tuition for the skill.
- [monitor] No interest in interactive games (peekaboo, give-and-take) plus no babble — a two-domain absence is worth a written note for the visit list.
- [call within 24h] New ear-infection signs — night waking with crying plus ear-pulling after congestion — or any illness that will not resolve.
- [call now] Head injury with vomiting, lethargy, or unequal pupils; fever ≥102°F rectal with lethargy; labored breathing — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Book the first-birthday photographer this week: candid-documentary style beats posed for one-year-olds, sessions run $400–1,500 for 60–90 minutes, and 2–4-month lead times make this the last comfortable week for May 11. Book a separate 15-minute everyone-in-frame slot — the cake photos crowd out the family photo otherwise.
- Play imitation games in both directions — copy his spoon-banging, then offer clap, wave, and stack-and-knock for him to copy back; imitation is the social-learning channel year 2 runs on. AAP: milestones at 12 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
- Set up in-and-out play: one wide container plus fist-sized safe objects — putting a block in a cup is a CDC 12-month checkpoint, and he will run the fill-and-dump loop for surprisingly long stretches. CDC 12-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Tape butcher paper to the floor and hand over one jumbo crayon — expect mouthing and a few accidental marks; this is grip and cause-and-effect practice, not art.

Upcoming
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — photographer confirmed this week; guest list and format locked by end of March.
- Day 344–351 (Apr 20–27, 2027): custom cake and smash-cake order window (2–3-week bakery lead) — calendar it now, and decide smash cake versus stacked-fruit alternative before ordering.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Stands alone for a few seconds
  AAP window: day 300-365
  What to look for: Often follows cruising. Balance precedes locomotion.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stands-briefly-no-support/complete

- Uses objects appropriately (cup, phone, book)
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Functional use — picks up phone and puts it to ear, holds book the right way. Pretend play emerges from here.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-objects-appropriately/complete

- Takes a few steps on her own
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: CDC checkpoint is 15 months. Wide normal range — late walking alone is not concerning if other milestones are on track.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-independent-steps/complete

- Uses one word besides mama or dada
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Commonly 'ball', 'dog', 'bye', or a family-specific word.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-one-word/complete

- Tries to imitate words you say
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Approximations count. 'Wa' for water is a real attempt.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tries-to-imitate-words/complete
